records.source: הַצַּדִּ֣יק אָבָ֔ד וְאֵ֥ין אִ֖ישׁ שָׂ֣ם עַל־לֵ֑ב וְאַנְשֵׁי־חֶ֤סֶד נֶֽאֱסָפִים֙ בְּאֵ֣ין מֵבִ֔ין כִּֽי־מִפְּנֵ֥י הָרָעָ֖ה נֶאֱסַ֥ף הַצַּדִּֽיק׃
records.gloss: The righteous [person] has perished, and there [is] not anyone [who] puts [it] on heart; and people of loyalty [are being] removed, when there [is] not [one who] has understanding that from before the evil he is removed, the righteous [person].
pieces: The righteous person perishes, \q and no one gives it a thought. \q Those who show loyal love are gathered away, and no one sees \q that the righteous is gathered away from the evil.

L.1: The righteous [one] perishes, \q and there is no one [who] lays [it] to heart; \q and {{gender:people|men}} of loyal love are taken away, while no one understands \q that from before the evil the righteous [one] is taken away.

R.1: Righteous people die, \q and no one cares. \q People who show faithful love are taken away, and no one understands why. \q They are taken away from all the evil.

decisions.choice: from before the evil: away from the evil, either the disaster to come or the wickedness of the time
decisions.reason: The phrase can mean that the righteous are spared the coming disaster by dying first (compare 2 Kings 22:20), or that they are swept away by the evil others do. Verse 2, which speaks of peace and rest, fits the first reading.

decisions.choice: taken away: gathered in death
decisions.reason: The verb means to gather. It is used of dying as being "gathered to one's people" (Genesis 25:8; 2 Kings 22:20).

decisions.choice: people of loyal love: the faithful, who keep covenant loyalty to God and to others
decisions.reason: The phrase describes people marked by steadfast faithfulness (Psalm 12:2; Micah 7:2, where the same complaint is made).

decisions.choice: people (setting: men)
decisions.reason: Men and women are both meant. Literal gives the inclusive form by default; Balanced and Readable use "those" and "people".

decisions.choice: no one understands why
decisions.reason: Readable shortens "no one understands that ..." to "why" and gives the reason in the next sentence.

records.heading: The righteous perish and the idols fail

records.source: יָב֣וֹא שָׁל֔וֹם יָנ֖וּחוּ עַל־מִשְׁכְּבוֹתָ֑ם הֹלֵ֖ךְ נְכֹחֽוֹ׃
records.gloss: He will go [into] peace; they will rest on their beds, [each one who] walks [in] his straightforwardness.
pieces: He goes in to peace. \q Those who walk the straight way find rest on their beds.

L.2: He enters into peace; \q they rest on their beds, \q [each one] walking [in] his uprightness.

R.2: Those who live honest lives will find peace. \q They rest in their graves as if asleep in bed.

decisions.choice: their beds: their resting places in death
decisions.reason: The word for bed is used of a bier or burial place (2 Chronicles 16:14; Ezekiel 32:25). The righteous who die are at rest, not lost.

decisions.choice: peace: rest and well-being after death
decisions.reason: To "go to one's fathers in peace" is a promise of a good death (Genesis 15:15; 2 Kings 22:20).

decisions.choice: he enters, they rest: the singular righteous one stands for all the righteous
decisions.reason: The verse moves from singular to plural. The last words, about each one who walks uprightly, describe them all.

decisions.choice: They rest in their graves as if asleep in bed
decisions.reason: Readable explains the picture of the bed as the grave.

records.source: וְאַתֶּ֥ם קִרְבוּ־הֵ֖נָּה בְּנֵ֣י עֹנְנָ֑ה זֶ֥רַע מְנָאֵ֖ף וַתִּזְנֶֽה׃
records.gloss: And you, draw near hither, O children of a soothsayer, offspring of an adulterer, and she has played the prostitute.
pieces: As for you, step up here, you children of a witch, \q you breed of an adulterer and a prostitute!

L.3: But you, draw near here, children of a sorceress, \q offspring of an adulterer and [of one who] plays the prostitute!

R.3: But you people, come here! You are like the children of a witch, \q born of a man who cheats on his wife and a woman who sells her body.

decisions.choice: children of a sorceress, offspring of an adulterer: people whose way of life is magic and unfaithfulness to God
decisions.reason: The names describe what the people are, not who their parents were. Turning to other gods is pictured as adultery and prostitution (1:21; Jeremiah 3:1-9; Hosea 2:4-7), and magic was forbidden (Deuteronomy 18:10-12).

decisions.choice: and plays the prostitute: the verb has an unexpected form
decisions.reason: The Hebrew verb reads "and she played the prostitute" (or "you played the prostitute"). It is taken as describing the mother, joined to "adulterer": the offspring of an adulterer and a prostitute.

decisions.choice: You are like; a man who cheats on his wife and a woman who sells her body
decisions.reason: Readable marks the names as a comparison and explains them in plain words.

records.source: עַל־מִי֙ תִּתְעַנָּ֔גוּ עַל־מִ֛י תַּרְחִ֥יבוּ פֶ֖ה תַּאֲרִ֣יכוּ לָשׁ֑וֹן הֲלֽוֹא־אַתֶּ֥ם יִלְדֵי־פֶ֖שַׁע זֶ֥רַע שָֽׁקֶר׃
records.gloss: On whom are you making fun? On whom do you make wide a mouth, do you make long a tongue? Not [are] you children of transgression, offspring of deception,
pieces: Who is it you are jeering at? \q At whom do you open your mouths wide and stick out your tongues? \q Are you not children born of rebellion, offspring of lies,

L.4: At whom do you make sport? \q Against whom do you open wide [your] mouth [and] stick out [your] tongue? \q Are you not children of transgression, offspring of deceit,

R.4: Who are you making fun of? \q Who are you making faces at and sticking out your tongues at? \q You are rebels and liars!

decisions.choice: opening the mouth wide and sticking out the tongue: gestures of scorn
decisions.reason: The gestures mock someone, perhaps the righteous of verse 1 or God's messengers (compare Psalm 22:8; 35:21).

decisions.choice: transgression: rebellion against God
decisions.reason: The word means a breaking away, rebellion against a lord (1:2, 28; 43:27).

decisions.choice: You are rebels and liars!
decisions.reason: Readable states the answer to the question as a plain sentence and ends it there, beginning verse 5 as new sentences.

records.source: הַנֵּֽחָמִים֙ בָּֽאֵלִ֔ים תַּ֖חַת כָּל־עֵ֣ץ רַעֲנָ֑ן שֹׁחֲטֵ֤י הַיְלָדִים֙ בַּנְּחָלִ֔ים תַּ֖חַת סְעִפֵ֥י הַסְּלָעִֽים׃
records.gloss: [who are] inflaming yourselves among oaks, under every tree luxuriant, slaughtering the children in the wadis, under the clefts of the cliffs?
pieces: you who inflame yourselves with lust among the oaks, \q under every leafy tree, \q who butcher children in the stream beds \q below the clefts of the cliffs?

L.5: [you who] inflame yourselves among the oaks, \q under every leafy tree, \q slaughtering the children in the wadis, \q under the clefts of the crags?

R.5: You burn with desire for false gods among the oak trees \q and under every leafy tree. \q You kill your children as sacrifices in the dry valleys \q under the rocky cliffs.

decisions.choice: under every leafy tree: the hill shrines where other gods were worshiped
decisions.reason: Green trees on hills were places for the worship of fertility gods, often with sexual rites (Deuteronomy 12:2; 1 Kings 14:23; Jeremiah 2:20; 3:6; Hosea 4:13). Oaks were part of the same worship in 1:29.

decisions.choice: slaughtering the children in the wadis: child sacrifice
decisions.reason: The law forbade giving children to other gods (Leviticus 18:21; Deuteronomy 12:31). Kings of Judah did it in the Valley of Hinnom outside Jerusalem (2 Kings 16:3; 21:6; 23:10; Jeremiah 7:31).

decisions.choice: inflame yourselves among the oaks: burn with desire in the worship at the sacred trees
decisions.reason: The verb means to grow hot. The word for oaks has the same letters as a word for gods, so the phrase may also be read "inflame yourselves with the gods" (as in 1:29, the word can mean great trees).

decisions.choice: burn with desire for false gods; kill your children as sacrifices
decisions.reason: Readable says plainly what the burning and the slaughter were for, following the meaning decisions.

records.source: בְּחַלְּקֵי־נַ֣חַל חֶלְקֵ֔ךְ הֵ֥ם הֵ֖ם גּוֹרָלֵ֑ךְ גַּם־לָהֶ֞ם שָׁפַ֥כְתְּ נֶ֨סֶךְ֙ הֶעֱלִ֣ית מִנְחָ֔ה הַ֥עַל אֵ֖לֶּה אֶנָּחֵֽם׃
records.gloss: Among [the] smooth [stones] of [the] wadi [is] your portion; they, they [are] your allotted portion; also to them you have poured out a drink offering; you have offered up a grain offering. On these [things] will I relent?
pieces: With the smooth stones of the stream bed lies your share; \q those, those are your allotment. \q Even to them you have poured out drink offerings and lifted up grain offerings. \q Am I to be soothed by this?

L.6: Among the smooth [stones] of the wadi [is] your portion; \q they, they [are] your lot; \q to them also you have poured out a drink offering; you have brought up a grain offering. \q Over these [things] should I relent?

R.6: You worship smooth stones from the dry stream beds. \q Those stones are all you will get. \q You pour out wine for them as an offering. You give them gifts of grain. \q Should I calmly accept all this?

decisions.choice: your portion, your lot: what you have chosen to belong to
decisions.reason: The words for "smooth stones" and "portion" sound alike. A portion and a lot are a share of land; the faithful say the LORD is their portion (Psalm 16:5; Jeremiah 10:16). These people have taken stones for their share instead.

decisions.choice: the smooth stones of the wadi: stones set up and worshiped
decisions.reason: Stones from a stream bed seem to have been used as objects of worship, given drink and grain offerings. What exactly they were is not known.

decisions.choice: should I relent: should I hold back and let this pass
decisions.reason: The verb can mean to be comforted or appeased, or to change one's mind about punishing (1:24). Either way the question expects the answer no.

decisions.choice: You worship; are all you will get; wine
decisions.reason: Readable says plainly that the stones were worshiped and names the drink offering as wine, which it usually was (Numbers 15:5).

records.source: עַ֤ל הַר־גָּבֹ֨הַּ֙ וְנִשָּׂ֔א שַׂ֖מְתְּ מִשְׁכָּבֵ֑ךְ גַּם־שָׁ֥ם עָלִ֖ית לִזְבֹּ֥חַ זָֽבַח׃
records.gloss: On a mountain high and lifted up you have set your bed; also there you have gone up to sacrifice a sacrifice.
pieces: On a mountain high and lifted up you have laid out your bed, \q and there too you have gone up to offer sacrifice.

L.7: On a mountain high and lifted up you have set your bed; \q there also you have gone up to sacrifice a sacrifice.

R.7: You have made your bed on a mountain that is high and lifted up, like a wife who is unfaithful to her husband. \q You went up there to offer sacrifices to false gods.

decisions.choice: you have set your bed: worship of other gods pictured as adultery
decisions.reason: The bed is the bed of an unfaithful wife; the high places where idols were worshiped are her meeting places (Jeremiah 3:2, 6; Ezekiel 16:16; 23:17).

decisions.choice: high and lifted up: the words used of the LORD in this book
decisions.reason: The same pair describes the Lord on his throne (6:1), the servant (52:13), and the LORD in verse 15 below. The people climb a lofty mountain for their idols, when the High and Lifted Up One is the LORD.

decisions.choice: like a wife who is unfaithful to her husband; to false gods
decisions.reason: Readable explains the picture of the bed and names those the sacrifices were for, following the meaning decision.

records.source: וְאַחַ֤ר הַדֶּ֨לֶת֙ וְהַמְּזוּזָ֔ה שַׂ֖מְתְּ זִכְרוֹנֵ֑ךְ כִּ֣י מֵאִתִּ֞י גִּלִּ֣ית וַֽתַּעֲלִ֗י הִרְחַ֤בְתְּ מִשְׁכָּבֵךְ֙ וַתִּכְרָת־לָ֣ךְ מֵהֶ֔ם אָהַ֥בְתְּ מִשְׁכָּבָ֖ם יָ֥ד חָזִֽית׃
records.gloss: And behind the door and the doorpost you have set up your memorial, for from with me you have uncovered and you have gone up; you have made wide your bed, and you have cut for yourself from them; you have loved their bed; a hand you have seen.
pieces: Behind the door and its doorpost \q you have put your reminder. \q You deserted {{deity_pronoun:me|Me}}: you stripped, climbed in, and made your bed wide. You struck a bargain with them for yourself; \q you loved their bed; you gazed at their nakedness.

L.8: And behind the door and the doorpost \q you have set up your memorial; \q for away from {{deity_pronoun:me|Me}} you have uncovered [yourself] and gone up; you have made your bed wide, and you have cut [a pact] for yourself with them; \q you have loved their bed; you have gazed on a hand.

R.8: You put symbols of your false gods behind your doors and doorposts. \q You left {{deity_pronoun:me|Me}}. You took off your clothes, climbed into your bed, and made room in it for your lovers. You made deals with them. \q You loved going to bed with them and looking at their naked bodies.

decisions.choice: your memorial behind the door and doorpost: a sign of other gods in the home
decisions.reason: Israel was told to write God's words on the doorposts as a reminder (Deuteronomy 6:9; 11:20). Here the reminder is of something else, an object or sign of other gods, kept out of sight behind the door.

decisions.choice: you have gazed on a hand: you looked with desire on their nakedness
decisions.reason: In this picture of adultery the "hand" is most likely a polite word for the male organ. The same word means a monument in 56:5, and it can also mean a place, so the phrase may mean you looked on their monument, an idol.

decisions.choice: you cut for yourself: you made an agreement, a covenant with them
decisions.reason: To "cut" is the usual verb for making a covenant (28:15). The object is left unstated: Israel made a pact with its lovers, the other gods or the nations that served them.

decisions.choice: symbols of your false gods; made room in it for your lovers
decisions.reason: Readable names what the memorial was and keeps the picture of the unfaithful wife, explaining it in plain words.

records.source: וַתָּשֻׁ֤רִי לַמֶּ֨לֶךְ֙ בַּשֶּׁ֔מֶן וַתַּרְבִּ֖י רִקֻּחָ֑יִךְ וַתְּשַׁלְּחִ֤י צִרַ֨יִךְ֙ עַד־מֵ֣רָחֹ֔ק וַתַּשְׁפִּ֖ילִי עַד־שְׁאֽוֹל׃
records.gloss: And you journeyed to the king with oil, and you increased your perfumes, and you sent your envoys to from a distance, and you showed abasement to Sheol.
pieces: You went to the king with olive oil \q and heaped up your perfumes. \q You sent your envoys far away, \q and you sank down as far as Sheol.

L.9: And you journeyed to the king with oil, \q and you multiplied your perfumes; \q and you sent your envoys far off, \q and you brought [yourself] low, down to Sheol.

R.9: You went to the king with olive oil and many perfumes as gifts. \q You sent your messengers to faraway places. \q You lowered yourself all the way down to the grave.

decisions.choice: the king: a human king, or the god Molech
decisions.reason: The word is "king". Its consonants are those of Molech, the god to whom children were sacrificed (Leviticus 18:21; 2 Kings 23:10), and verse 5 has just spoken of child sacrifice, so the verse may be about a god. It may also be about a foreign king whose help Judah sought with gifts, as in 30:1-7. Which is meant is uncertain.

decisions.choice: you brought yourself low, down to Sheol: you went to any depth, as far as the realm of the dead
decisions.reason: The verb means to make low. Seeking help so far and so low may also point to consulting the dead (8:19; 28:15).

decisions.choice: as gifts
decisions.reason: Readable says what the oil and perfumes were for.

records.source: בְּרֹ֤ב דַּרְכֵּךְ֙ יָגַ֔עַתְּ לֹ֥א אָמַ֖רְתְּ נוֹאָ֑שׁ חַיַּ֤ת יָדֵךְ֙ מָצָ֔את עַל־כֵּ֖ן לֹ֥א חָלִֽית׃
records.gloss: With the greatness of your way you became weary; not you said, despairing; [the] life of your hand you found; therefore not you became weak.
pieces: You wore yourself out with all your traveling, \q yet you never said, "It is no use." \q Your arm found fresh life, \q so you did not give way.

L.10: With the length of your way you grew weary, \q [yet] you did not say, "[It is] hopeless"; \q you found life [for] your hand; \q therefore you did not grow faint.

R.10: Your long journeys made you tired, \q but you would not admit that it was hopeless. \q You found new energy, \q so you did not give up.

decisions.choice: the life of your hand: renewed strength
decisions.reason: The hand stands for strength. The people kept finding the energy to go on chasing other gods and helpers.

decisions.choice: you did not say, It is hopeless: you never gave up your own way
decisions.reason: Exhausted as they were, they would not admit their search was useless and turn back (compare Jeremiah 2:25; 18:12).

records.source: וְאֶת־מִ֞י דָּאַ֤גְתְּ וַתִּֽירְאִי֙ כִּ֣י תְכַזֵּ֔בִי וְאוֹתִי֙ לֹ֣א זָכַ֔רְתְּ לֹא־שַׂ֖מְתְּ עַל־לִבֵּ֑ךְ הֲלֹ֨א אֲנִ֤י מַחְשֶׁה֙ וּמֵ֣עֹלָ֔ם וְאוֹתִ֖י לֹ֥א תִירָֽאִי׃
records.gloss: And whom did you dread and did you fear, that you will lie, and me not you remembered, not you put [it] on your heart? Not I [have been] silent, and from long ago, and me not you fear?
pieces: Whom did you dread so much, whom did you fear, that you turned false, \q and did not remember {{deity_pronoun:me|Me}} or give {{deity_pronoun:me|Me}} a thought? \q Was it that I stayed silent so long \q that you no longer fear {{deity_pronoun:me|Me}}?

L.11: And whom did you dread and fear, that you lied, \q and {{deity_pronoun:me|Me}} you did not remember, \q [nor] did you lay [it] on your heart? \q Have I not [been] silent, even from long ago, \q and {{deity_pronoun:me|Me}} you do not fear?

R.11: Who frightened you so much that you lied to {{deity_pronoun:me|Me}}? \q You forgot all about {{deity_pronoun:me|Me}}. \q You did not even think about {{deity_pronoun:me|Me}}. \q I have been quiet for a long time. \q Is that why you do not fear {{deity_pronoun:me|Me}}?

decisions.choice: that you lie: that you were false to God
decisions.reason: The verb means to lie or deceive. The fear of others led them to break faith with the LORD and trust other helpers.

decisions.choice: have I not been silent, and from long ago: God's long patience mistaken for absence
decisions.reason: God held back from punishing, and the people took his silence to mean he need not be feared (42:14; Psalm 50:21).

decisions.choice: turned false; lied to me
decisions.reason: Balanced and Readable make clear that the lie was faithlessness toward God, following the meaning decision.

records.source: אֲנִ֥י אַגִּ֖יד צִדְקָתֵ֑ךְ וְאֶֽת־מַעֲשַׂ֖יִךְ וְלֹ֥א יוֹעִילֽוּךְ׃
records.gloss: I, I will declare your righteousness and your deeds, and they will not benefit you.
pieces: I will lay bare what you call your righteousness, \q and your deeds as well; they will be of no use to you.

L.12: I will declare your righteousness \q and your deeds, and they will not profit you.

R.12: I will show everyone the righteousness you claim \q and the things you have done. None of it will help you.

decisions.choice: your righteousness: the people's own claim to be in the right, spoken in irony
decisions.reason: God will make known what their righteousness really is, and it will be shown to be worthless (compare 58:2; 64:5).

decisions.choice: your deeds will not profit you: their works cannot save them
decisions.reason: The deeds include the idols they made; the same verb is used of idols that do not profit in 44:9-10.

decisions.choice: what you call; you claim
decisions.reason: Balanced and Readable mark the irony that Literal leaves to the reader.

records.source: בְּזַֽעֲקֵךְ֙ יַצִּילֻ֣ךְ קִבּוּצַ֔יִךְ וְאֶת־כֻּלָּ֥ם יִשָּׂא־ר֖וּחַ יִקַּח־הָ֑בֶל וְהַחוֹסֶ֥ה בִי֙ יִנְחַל־אֶ֔רֶץ וְיִירַ֖שׁ הַר־קָדְשִֽׁי׃
records.gloss: When you cry out, let them deliver you, your collections; and all of them a wind will carry away, a breath will take [them] away; and the [one who] takes refuge in me will inherit [the] land and will possess the mountain of my holiness.
pieces: When you call for help, let your crowd of idols rescue you! \q The wind will sweep every one of them away; a puff of air will carry them off. \q But whoever takes shelter in {{deity_pronoun:me|Me}} will receive the land as an inheritance \q and will own {{deity_pronoun:my|My}} holy mountain.

L.13: When you cry out, let your collections [of idols] deliver you! \q But the wind will carry them all off; a breath will take [them] away. \q But the one who takes refuge in {{deity_pronoun:me|Me}} will inherit [the] land \q and possess {{deity_pronoun:my|My}} holy mountain.

R.13: When you cry for help, see if your many idols will save you! \q The wind will blow them all away. Just a breath will carry them off. \q But people who come to {{deity_pronoun:me|Me}} for safety will receive the land. \q My holy mountain will be theirs.

decisions.choice: your collections: the heap of idols the people have gathered
decisions.reason: The word occurs only here and means a gathering or collection. In context it is the many idols and gods they have collected.

decisions.choice: a breath: a mere puff of air, something empty and passing
decisions.reason: The same word is the "vapor" of Ecclesiastes 1:2 and is used of idols as empty things (Jeremiah 10:15).

decisions.choice: the one who takes refuge in me will inherit the land: the promise passes to those who trust God
decisions.reason: The land and the holy mountain go not to the idol worshipers but to those who seek shelter in the LORD (Psalm 37:9, 11; compare 65:9).

decisions.choice: see if your many idols will save you
decisions.reason: Readable turns the mocking command into a challenge, keeping its irony.

records.source: וְאָמַ֥ר סֹֽלּוּ־סֹ֖לּוּ פַּנּוּ־דָ֑רֶךְ הָרִ֥ימוּ מִכְשׁ֖וֹל מִדֶּ֥רֶךְ עַמִּֽי׃ס
records.gloss: And someone will say: cast up, cast up, make clear [the] way, lift up stumbling block[s] from the way of my people.
pieces: Then the word will go out: "Raise a highway, raise it up, clear a path! \q Lift every stumbling block out of the road {{deity_pronoun:my|My}} people travel."

L.14: And [one] will say, "Build up, build up, clear [the] way; \q lift [the] stumbling block out of the way of {{deity_pronoun:my|My}} people."

R.14: Someone will say, "Build a road! Build it up! Get it ready! \q Take away everything that could make {{deity_pronoun:my|My}} people trip as they travel home."

decisions.choice: build up, clear the way: prepare a road for God's people to return
decisions.reason: The call echoes 40:3 and returns in 62:10, where a highway is built up for the people coming home.

decisions.choice: someone will say: the speaker is not named
decisions.reason: The verb has no stated subject. A voice, perhaps God's or a herald's, gives the order; "my people" shows the words come from God (compare 40:1-3).

decisions.choice: stumbling block: anything that makes the people fall
decisions.reason: After the idolatry described in verses 3-13, the obstacles may include the sins that kept the people from God (compare 8:14).

decisions.choice: as they travel home
decisions.reason: Readable says where the road leads, following the allusion to 40:3 and 62:10.

records.source: כִּי֩ כֹ֨ה אָמַ֜ר רָ֣ם וְנִשָּׂ֗א שֹׁכֵ֥ן עַד֙ וְקָד֣וֹשׁ שְׁמ֔וֹ מָר֥וֹם וְקָד֖וֹשׁ אֶשְׁכּ֑וֹן וְאֶת־דַּכָּא֙ וּשְׁפַל־ר֔וּחַ לְהַחֲיוֹת֙ ר֣וּחַ שְׁפָלִ֔ים וּֽלְהַחֲי֖וֹת לֵ֥ב נִדְכָּאִֽים׃
records.gloss: For thus says [the] high and lifted up [one], [who] dwells [in] perpetuity, and holy [is] his name: [in a] high place and holy I dwell, and with [the] crushed and lowly of spirit, to restore [the] spirit of [the] lowly and to restore [the] heart of [the] crushed.
pieces: For the One high and lifted up, who dwells in eternity, whose name is Holy, says this: \q My home is the high and holy place, \q yet I am also with the one who is crushed and low in spirit, \q to bring the spirit of the lowly back to life \q and put new life into the hearts of the crushed.

L.15: For thus says the high and lifted up [One], who dwells [in] eternity, and Holy [is] {{deity_pronoun:his|His}} name: \q [In the] high and holy [place] I dwell, \q and with the crushed and lowly of spirit, \q to revive the spirit of the lowly \q and to revive the heart of the crushed.

R.15: The God who is high and lifted up lives forever. His name is Holy. This is what {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} says: \q I live in a high and holy place. \q But I also live with people who are crushed and humble. \q I give new life to people who are humble. \q I give new courage to people whose hearts are broken.

decisions.choice: high and lifted up: the LORD seen by Isaiah on his throne
decisions.reason: The same pair of words describes the Lord in 6:1 and the servant in 52:13. In verse 7 the people climbed a mountain "high and lifted up" for their idols; here the One who is truly high speaks.

decisions.choice: who dwells in eternity: who lives forever, or who is enthroned in eternity
decisions.reason: The verb means to dwell, and the noun means lasting time. The phrase can describe God as living forever or as dwelling in eternity as his home.

decisions.choice: I dwell on high, and with the crushed and lowly: the holy God is near the humble
decisions.reason: The God who is beyond all heights makes his home with those who are broken and humble (66:1-2; Psalm 34:19; 51:19; 138:6).

decisions.choice: crushed: broken, humbled by trouble or sorrow for sin
decisions.reason: The word means crushed to dust. It describes people who have been humbled, and so are open to God.

decisions.choice: His name is Holy; I give new courage to people whose hearts are broken
decisions.reason: Readable breaks the verse into short sentences and explains reviving the heart as giving new courage.

records.heading: The high God with the crushed and lowly

records.source: כִּ֣י לֹ֤א לְעוֹלָם֙ אָרִ֔יב וְלֹ֥א לָנֶ֖צַח אֶקְּצ֑וֹף כִּי־ר֨וּחַ֙ מִלְּפָנַ֣י יַֽעֲט֔וֹף וּנְשָׁמ֖וֹת אֲנִ֥י עָשִֽׂיתִי׃
records.gloss: For not forever will I conduct a case, and not to perpetuity will I be angry, for [the] spirit from before me would grow faint, and [the] breaths [which] I, I made.
pieces: For I will not press {{deity_pronoun:my|My}} case forever, \q nor stay angry for all time; \q otherwise the human spirit would grow faint before {{deity_pronoun:me|Me}}, \q the breath of life that I {{deity_pronoun:myself|Myself}} made.

L.16: For I will not contend forever, \q and I will not be angry to perpetuity; \q for [the] spirit would grow faint before {{deity_pronoun:me|Me}}, \q and the breaths [that] I {{deity_pronoun:myself|Myself}} made.

R.16: I will not keep accusing {{deity_pronoun:my|My}} people forever. \q I will not always be angry. \q If I did, the people I created would grow weak and die before {{deity_pronoun:me|Me}}.

decisions.choice: I will not contend forever: God's anger has a limit
decisions.reason: God's case against his people does not last forever (Psalm 103:9; compare 54:7-8).

decisions.choice: for the spirit would grow faint: if God's anger went on, the life he gave would fail
alternatives: for the spirit goes forth from me
decisions.reason: The words give the reason God stops: his creatures could not survive endless anger. They may also be read "for the spirit goes out from me", speaking of the life God gives.

decisions.choice: the breaths I made: the breath of life God gives
decisions.reason: God breathed life into the first man (Genesis 2:7) and gives breath to all people on the earth (42:5).

decisions.choice: my people; the people I created would grow weak and die
decisions.reason: Readable names those God contends with and explains the faint spirit and the breaths as people losing their life.

records.source: בַּעֲוֺ֥ן בִּצְע֛וֹ קָצַ֥פְתִּי וְאַכֵּ֖הוּ הַסְתֵּ֣ר וְאֶקְצֹ֑ף וַיֵּ֥לֶךְ שׁוֹבָ֖ב בְּדֶ֥רֶךְ לִבּֽוֹ׃
records.gloss: In the iniquity of his unjust gain I was angry, and I struck him; I hid and I was angry; and he walked apostate in the way of his own heart.
pieces: Because of his sinful greed I was angry; I struck him, hid {{deity_pronoun:my|My}} face, and was angry still. \q Yet he kept turning away, going the way his own heart chose.

L.17: Because of the iniquity of his unjust gain I was angry, and I struck him; I hid [{{deity_pronoun:my|My}} face] and was angry; \q and he went on, turning away, in the way of his [own] heart.

R.17: I was angry because {{deity_pronoun:my|My}} people were greedy and sinful. I punished them. I turned away from them in anger. \q But they kept going their own way and did what they wanted.

decisions.choice: him, he: the people of Israel, spoken of as one person
decisions.reason: The singular refers to the people as a whole, as "my people" in verse 14.

decisions.choice: I hid: I hid my face, withdrew my presence and help
decisions.reason: The verb stands alone, but the full phrase "hide the face" is common for God's withdrawing in anger (8:17; 54:8; 59:2).

decisions.choice: turning away: going back from God, faithless
decisions.reason: The word describes a people who turn back from following God (Jeremiah 3:14, 22).

decisions.choice: hid my face; turned away from them
decisions.reason: Balanced supplies the object of "hid"; Readable says what hiding the face means.

decisions.choice: my people, them, they
decisions.reason: Readable names the people and uses plural pronouns.

records.source: דְּרָכָ֥יו רָאִ֖יתִי וְאֶרְפָּאֵ֑הוּ וְאַנְחֵ֕הוּ וַאֲשַׁלֵּ֧ם נִֽחֻמִ֛ים ל֖וֹ וְלַאֲבֵלָֽיו׃
records.gloss: His ways I have seen, and I will heal him; and I will lead him, and I will restore comforts to him and to his mourners.
pieces: I have seen the paths he has taken, but I will heal him. \q I will guide him \q and give back comfort to him, and to those among his people who mourn.

L.18: I have seen his ways, and I will heal him; \q and I will lead him, \q and I will restore comfort to him and to his mourners.

R.18: I have seen what {{deity_pronoun:my|My}} people have done. But I will heal them. \q I will lead them and comfort them again. \q I will comfort those who are sad.

decisions.choice: I have seen his ways, and I will heal him: grace after judgment
decisions.reason: God has seen the stubborn ways of verse 17, yet he chooses to heal (30:26; Hosea 14:5, which is 14:4 in some Bibles).

decisions.choice: restore comfort: make good, give back comfort in full
decisions.reason: The verb means to repay or make whole. The comfort promised in 40:1 is given back to those who have suffered.

decisions.choice: his mourners: those in Israel who grieve
decisions.reason: The mourners may be those who grieve over Zion's ruin or over sin (61:2-3; 66:10).

decisions.choice: what my people have done; them
decisions.reason: Readable names the people and uses plural pronouns, as in verse 17.

records.source: בּוֹרֵ֖א נִ֣יב שְׂפָתָ֑יִם שָׁל֨וֹם׀שָׁל֜וֹם לָרָח֧וֹק וְלַקָּר֛וֹב אָמַ֥ר יְהוָ֖ה וּרְפָאתִֽיו׃
records.gloss: [I am] creating [the] fruit of [the] lips: peace, peace to the far [one] and to the near [one], says Yahweh, and I will heal him.
pieces: I bring into being the fruit of the lips: \q Peace, peace, to those far off and to those close at hand, says {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}}, and I will heal them.

L.19: [I am] creating [the] fruit of [the] lips: \q Peace, peace to the far and to the near, says {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}}, and I will heal him.

R.19: I am giving people new words to speak: \q Peace, peace to those who are far away and to those who are near! I will heal them, says {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}}.

decisions.choice: peace, peace to the far and to the near: peace offered to all
decisions.reason: In this chapter the far may be the scattered exiles and the near those still in the land. Paul takes up the words in Ephesians 2:17 (and 2:13) of Christ bringing peace to Gentiles who were far off and to Jews who were near.

decisions.choice: the fruit of the lips: what the lips produce, words of praise and thanks
decisions.reason: The phrase means speech, and here most likely praise (Hosea 14:3; Hebrews 13:15). God himself creates the words his people will speak.

decisions.choice: peace, peace: complete peace
decisions.reason: Doubling the word makes it full and certain (26:3).

decisions.choice: I will heal him: the people, as in verse 18
decisions.reason: The singular "him" refers to the people as one, or to each person far and near.

decisions.choice: them
decisions.reason: Balanced and Readable use the plural for the people; Literal keeps "him".

decisions.choice: I am giving people new words to speak
decisions.reason: Readable explains "creating the fruit of the lips".

records.source: וְהָרְשָׁעִ֖ים כַּיָּ֣ם נִגְרָ֑שׁ כִּ֤י הַשְׁקֵט֙ לֹ֣א יוּכָ֔ל וַיִּגְרְשׁ֥וּ מֵימָ֖יו רֶ֥פֶשׁ וָטִֽיט׃
records.gloss: And the wicked [people] [are] like [the] sea [which is] tossed, for to be quiet not it is able, and they toss up its waters mire and mud.
pieces: But the wicked are like the churning sea \q that can never lie calm; \q its waters cast up muck and mud.

L.20: But the wicked [are] like the tossing sea, \q for it cannot be quiet, \q and its waters toss up mire and mud.

R.20: But people who do evil are like a stormy sea. \q It can never be calm. \q Its waves keep stirring up mud and dirt.

decisions.choice: like the tossing sea: always restless, never at peace
decisions.reason: The restless sea pictures the inner turmoil of the wicked, in contrast to the peace of verse 19 (compare Jude 13).

decisions.choice: mire and mud: the filth the sea throws up
decisions.reason: What comes out of the wicked is like the dirt the waves churn up from below.

records.source: אֵ֣ין שָׁל֔וֹם אָמַ֥ר אֱלֹהַ֖י לָרְשָׁעִֽים׃ס
records.gloss: There is not peace, says my God, for the wicked.
pieces: There is no peace, \q says my God, for the wicked.

L.21: There is no peace, \q says my God, for the wicked.

R.21: There is no peace for people who do evil, \q says my God.

decisions.choice: there is no peace for the wicked: the same closing warning as 48:22
decisions.reason: The words repeat 48:22, with "my God" in place of "the LORD". With 66:24 they mark the ends of the last sections of the book. The peace offered in verse 19 is not for those who go on in wickedness.

decisions.choice: my God: the prophet speaks of God as his own
decisions.reason: Here the prophet names the speaker as "my God", where 48:22 has "the LORD".
